findings.explanation: Systolic BP at SITE-C has SD 3.6 versus 13.9 at the other sites (variance ratio 0.07, p=7.7e-172). Real patient data are rarely this uniform.
findings.recommendedReviewAction: Check whether readings were copied, templated or entered without measurement.

findings.explanation: 89% of systolic BP readings at SITE-C end in 0 or 5 (about 20% expected if last digits were uniform; n=480, p=3.9e-230). This suggests rounded or invented values.
findings.recommendedReviewAction: Request source documents or device logs for a sample of readings.

findings.explanation: SITE-C has 18 entries made >24 h after the visit (3.8% of 480) versus 0.0% at the other sites (p=7.4e-12).
findings.recommendedReviewAction: Review the affected visits and the site's data-entry practices.

findings.explanation: SITE-C has 18 entries made late at night (3.8% of 480) versus 0.0% at the other sites (p=7.4e-12).
findings.recommendedReviewAction: Review the affected visits and the site's data-entry practices.

findings.explanation: Participant recording profiles at SITE-C score higher on the unsupervised anomaly model than at the other sites (mean 0.49 vs 0.46, p=3.5e-10). This is an anomaly signal, not proof of fraud.
findings.recommendedReviewAction: Use alongside the site-level statistics; do not act on this score alone.

findings.explanation: SITE-C has 18 completed visits without OTP verification (3.8% of 480) versus 0.6% at the other sites (p=3.5e-06).
findings.recommendedReviewAction: Review the affected visits and the site's data-entry practices.
